scalars.scalar_value: This is a full-time career appointment, exempt (monthly paid) from overtime pay.
Experience fundraising within a university, national laboratory, federally funded research institution, or similarly regulated environment.
Experience contributing to the growth of a foundation or institutional giving program, or a demonstrated interest in pipeline-building work.

items.item_text: This position is subject to a background check. Any convictions will be evaluated to determine if they directly relate to the responsibilities and requirements of the position. Having a conviction history will not automatically disqualify an applicant from being considered for employment.

This position is eligible for a hybrid work schedule - a combination of teleworking and performing work on site at Lawrence Berkeley National Lab, 1 Cyclotron Road, Berkeley, CA. Work schedules are dependent on business needs. Individuals working a hybrid schedule must reside within 150 miles of Berkeley Lab.

Bachelor's degree and a minimum of 5 years of progressively responsible fundraising experience, including experience raising funds for science, research, or technical programs, and demonstrated success securing foundation and/or corporate grants (or an equivalent combination of education and experience).
Experience contributing to the growth of a foundation or institutional giving program, or a demonstrated interest in pipeline-building work.
Experience fundraising within a university, national laboratory, federally funded research institution, or similarly regulated environment.
Track record of securing grants in the five- to six-figure range, and ideally direct experience with $1-million+ awards.
Experience working directly with scientists or technical staff to shape funding proposals.
Experience with Salesforce NPSP, Google Workspace, and Microsoft Office.

Partner with the Chief Development Officer, Lab leadership, and Principal Investigators to translate cutting-edge research priorities into compelling, fundable cases for support tailored to foundation and institutional audiences.
Connect scientists and program leads across the Lab to surface collaborative, cross-disciplinary funding opportunities that resonate with institutional funders.
Draft and manage proposals, letters of inquiry, and stewardship reports that keep funders engaged and informed.
Partner with the Lab's contracts, financial, and operations teams to ensure funds are accepted and managed appropriately.
Contribute to the Berkeley Lab Foundation's strategy for growing its foundation and institutional giving pipeline.
Help grow a robust pipeline of foundations, corporate giving programs, and institutional funders aligned with Berkeley Lab's research mission.
Research and help design targeted engagement strategies aimed at securing grants from the low six figures up to $1 million and beyond.
Manage a personal portfolio of foundation and institutional prospects through the full development cycle — from identification, cultivation, solicitation to stewardship.
Build relationships with foundation and corporate giving officers to elevate Berkeley Lab's visibility and priorities.
Support design and execution of donor engagement activities – meetings, tours, and outreach materials – in collaboration with Berkeley Lab leadership and scientists.
Help ensure foundation and institutional philanthropy aligns with DOE, UC, and IRS regulations, collaborating with Berkeley Lab, UC, and legal teams on gift and grant agreements.
Build connections with development colleagues across UC and partner institutions to strengthen collaborative fundraising.
Comfort operating with a good deal of autonomy on a small team, including a willingness to handle both relationship-building and hands-on administrative aspects of the work.
Familiarity with DOE, UC, or comparable government contracting and gift-acceptance policies.
Demonstrated ability to support the full donor development cycle – identification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship – along with strong research and analytical skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex scientific and technical work into clear, compelling proposals for institutional funders.
High level of initiative, attention to detail, and ability to manage multiple overlapping priorities independently.
Ability to travel occasionally and to work flexible hours, including occasional evenings or weekends for donor events.
